xia-chao opened PR #14391 from xia-chao:fix-fuel-buffer-flush-on-exit to bytecodealliance:main:

Instantiation-time fuel is dropped for modules with no start function.

A module with a multi-op const-expr global initializer reports 1 unit of fuel
consumed instead of 4. Adding an empty start function to the same module makes it
report the expected 6.

Those charges accumulate in fuel_consumed. Wasm functions fold that buffer into
fuel_var through the trailing end operator, but the module startup function is
synthesized and has no end, and module_start, the other place that flushes the
buffer, is only emitted when start exists. So the buffer is dropped.

fuel_function_exit now folds the buffer before saving. For functions translated
from wasm this is a no-op.

<details>
<summary>Screenshots from a debugger session on main (5877086436)</summary>

Breakpoint in fuel_function_exit, where fuel_consumed is 3 but only fuel_var
gets saved:

![breakpoint in fuel_function_exit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xia-chao/bughunt-shots/main/wasmtime/14203/01-fuel-function-exit.webp)

Breakpoint in module_start, the only place that folds the buffer. The frame above
it is func_environ.rs:6015, the module_start call guarded by
if let Some(start_func):

![breakpoint in module_start](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xia-chao/bughunt-shots/main/wasmtime/14203/02-module-start-flush.webp)

Same module, same initializer: fuel consumed = 1 without start, 6 with it.

![Debug Console](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xia-chao/bughunt-shots/main/wasmtime/14203/03-debug-console.webp)

</details>

Fixes #14203.
